visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 accurately depicts the projectile setup with axes, parabolic trajectory, launch angle/vector components, and correct flight-time equations, whereas Lesson 1 is mostly decorative and its mid-lesson scale/labels are ambiguous or incorrect relative to the actual 40 m/s at 30° range problem.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 2 includes a functional fill-in gate with a real prompt, accepted answer, hint, remediation path, and wiring after act_decomposition, while Lesson 1 has no available gate specs or plan and therefore no evidence of any functioning checkpoint.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 2 has clear, natural, well-paced narration with spoken math rendered appropriately, while Lesson 1 has no transcript available and therefore cannot demonstrate any narration quality.

sync.rationale: Lesson 2 at least provides visual cues that generally track the narrated references, despite a few cues firing somewhat early, whereas Lesson 1 has no transcript or timing data at all and therefore shows no evidence of synchronized visual changes.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 gives a mathematically correct and pedagogically clear decomposition of projectile motion, solves flight time and horizontal range appropriately, while Lesson 1 has no available transcript or lesson content to verify accuracy or learner support.

polish.rationale: Lesson 1 has a much more visually polished, cohesive, and legible presentation with strong centering and consistent cinematic styling, whereas Lesson 2’s mid-lesson layout is cluttered, low-contrast on the graph, and appears partially cropped/overlapped near the top.

aggregator.explanation: Lesson 2 is the clear overall winner: five of six agents favored it, all with high confidence, across the most instructionally important dimensions—visual accuracy, interactivity, narration quality, synchronization, and concept accuracy. These agents consistently noted that Lesson 2 provides correct projectile-motion diagrams, a functioning interactive checkpoint, clear narration, synchronized visual support, and mathematically accurate problem solving. Lesson 1 won only on polish, with moderate-high confidence, due to its more cohesive visual styling, but this does not outweigh Lesson 2’s strong advantages in correctness, pedagogy, narration, and interactivity.
